finding: Country-years 2000-2024: institutional quality (WGI voice, rule of law, corruption control, effectiveness; 0-1) is associated with fewer conflict onsets after controlling for access to basic services; access is not significant once institutions are included
citation: This study, v91/institutions/panel.py (UCDP/PRIO ACD v25.1; World Bank WGI and WDI)
notes: 3,663 country-years at peace, 98 onsets; a 0.1 rise in Q is associated with ~34% lower odds; same result with log GDP per capita; correlation of the two predictors 0.58

finding: Neither living standards nor institutional quality predicts when a conflict ends
citation: This study, panel.py
notes: 694 conflict-years and 94 endings

finding: A recent conflict (past 10 years) multiplies onset odds
citation: This study, panel.py
notes: the conflict trap

finding: Rapid institutional improvement before onset: no clear association in WGI data
citation: This study, panel.py
notes: inconclusive; risk of transitions kept as an assumption from the literature below

finding: Historical pace of institutional change (10-year changes 2004-2024): median ~0; top quarter +0.032; top tenth +0.062; top twentieth +0.084; one in three gains reversed the next decade
citation: This study, panel.py (World Bank WGI)
notes: 388 country-decades; 87 decades of gain > 0.02

finding: Even the fastest-transforming countries took 15-30 years to go from fragile to functioning institutional performance; fastest-20 pace: military in politics 17 yrs, government effectiveness 36, rule of law 41, control of corruption 27
citation: World Bank (2011) World Development Report 2011, Overview and Table 2.1 (Pritchett & de Weijer 2010)
notes: consistent with the model's top-tenth/top-twentieth paces (35-47 years for a typical fragile country)

finding: Worse governance than income would predict raises civil-war onset risk in the next 5-10 years (CPIA, WGI, ICRG)
citation: Fearon J. (2011) Governance and Civil War Onset, WDR 2011 background paper; also Revue d'economie du developpement 19(4)
notes: matches the panel of this study

finding: Groups excluded from central power (especially recently downgraded) more often start conflict with the government
citation: Cederman L.-E., Wimmer A. & Min B. (2010) World Politics 62(1):87-119
notes: effect size not verified

finding: Growing accommodation (group rights, autonomy, inclusion in power) plausibly explains the post-Cold-War decline of ethnic civil war
citation: Cederman L.-E., Gleditsch K.S. & Wucherpfennig J. (2017) J. Peace Research 54(2):262-274

finding: The more dimensions of power sharing (political territorial military economic) a settlement includes the more likely peace endures
citation: Hartzell C. & Hoddie M. (2003) AJPS 47(2):318-332
notes: small sample

finding: Institutions that constrain elites are the primary determinant of repeat civil war
citation: Walter B. (2015) J. Conflict Resolution 59(7):1242-1272

finding: Conflict risk falls faster after conflict in well-governed countries; holds beyond economic development
citation: Hegre H. & Nygard H.M. (2015) J. Conflict Resolution 59(6):984-1016

finding: Intermediate regimes are the most civil-war-prone; political change in either direction is associated with violence
citation: Hegre H., Ellingsen T., Gates S. & Gleditsch N.P. (2001) APSR 95(1):33-48
notes: basis of the reform-tension assumption

finding: Onset of democratisation predicts civil-war onset (conflicts over government); autocratisation similar and more abrupt
citation: Cederman L.-E., Hug S. & Krebs L. (2010) J. Peace Research 47(4):377-394
notes: authors: mechanisms unconfirmed

finding: Randomised community education in alternative dispute resolution (Liberia, 86 of 246 towns): land disputes resolved +7.3 pp; violent land disputes -19 pp (-41%); spillovers to untrained residents
citation: Blattman C., Hartman A. & Blair R. (2014) APSR 108(1):100-120
notes: side effects: more extrajudicial punishment (witch hunts 1.5% to 3.8%), more violent strikes; gains faded by 3 years and favoured the politically connected; cost US$1.2 m, about US$946 per violent act averted

finding: Mediation raises short-term agreements and crisis abatement; heavy-handed mediation is followed by more relapse later (the mediation dilemma)
citation: Beardsley K. et al. (2006) JCR 50(1):58-86; Beardsley K. (2011) The Mediation Dilemma, Cornell UP
notes: basis of the mediation relapse penalty

finding: Peacekeepers reduce the hazard of renewed war by more than 55% (115 civil wars 1944-1997)
citation: Fortna V.P. (2004) International Studies Quarterly 48(2):269-292
notes: mainly post-Cold War; selection into hard cases

finding: More UN troops are associated with fewer battle deaths (2014) and with fewer civilians targeted (2013)

notes: possible reverse causality

finding: GoBifo (Sierra Leone, randomised, pre-analysis plan): short-run public goods but no lasting change in institutions, collective action or inclusion of women and youth

finding: Liberia CDR raised cooperation in public-goods games (+6.5 pp; sensitive to specification); 2015: only in mixed-gender settings
